corrections.original_statement: shareholder approval is a live condition, not a formality.
corrections.corrected_state: Package 2 pre-emption waiver was announced on 10 July 2026. The combined circular and prospectus was published on 24 July 2026. The shareholder resolution passed on 11 August 2026 with 99.97% voting in favour (~997 million votes). On 12 August 2026, EnQuest announced that all conditions precedent had been satisfied, including PETRONAS Farmout Approval. Legal completion remains scheduled for 31 December 2026.
corrections.reason: The original publication on 27 October 2026 described shareholder approval as open even though that condition had already been completed in August 2026.
corrections.consequence: Readers received a stale transaction state for the deal described as the issue's most important transaction.
evidence: EnQuest PLC RNS Announcement: Package 2 Pre-emption Waiver (10 July 2026)
EnQuest PLC Combined Circular and Prospectus (24 July 2026)
EnQuest PLC General Meeting Results: 99.97% Approval (11 August 2026)
EnQuest PLC RNS: Satisfaction of All Conditions Precedent (12 August 2026)

corrections.original_statement: On completion EnQuest assumes a portfolio producing more than 100,000 boe/d.
corrections.corrected_state: The acquired Malaysian interests are expected to add approximately 57.4 kboepd. The figure of 'more than 100,000 boe/d' refers to the enlarged EnQuest group post-acquisition (UK North Sea + Malaysia), not production attributable to the acquired Malaysian assets alone.
corrections.reason: The publication conflated acquired-asset production with enlarged-group production.
corrections.consequence: The sentence overstated the production represented by the acquired portfolio and could distort transaction and asset valuation interpretation.
evidence: EnQuest Combined Circular and Prospectus (24 July 2026, Part I)

corrections.original_statement: Watchlist focused on expected completion on 31 December 2026 but omitted the separate economic effective date and expected readmission.
corrections.corrected_state: Expected legal completion: 31 December 2026; economic effective date: 1 January 2027; expected readmission: on or around 4 January 2027.
corrections.reason: These are distinct transaction milestones and must not be collapsed into one date.
corrections.consequence: Readers lacked visibility on the separate economic cutoff date versus legal and market readmission dates.
evidence: EnQuest Combined Circular and Prospectus (24 July 2026, Transaction Timetable)
next_signals: any variance from the stated dates

corrections.original_statement: local knowledge, on a short clock, from someone who was in the room when the decisions were made.
corrections.corrected_state: Under editorial review by sovereign authority ARIF. Proposed replacement: 'Every operator transition creates demand for rapidly assembled local context: public regulatory history, basin knowledge, asset chronology and disciplined interpretation.' Original PDF preserved immutable; sentence flagged and withheld from derivative summaries, metadata, and structured data pending Arif's explicit decision.
corrections.reason: The sentence may reasonably be read as implying non-public or internal access concerning a PETRONAS transaction, while the Method statement says that nothing in the issue comes from a non-public source.
corrections.consequence: Risk of implying non-public access. Bounded proposed replacement staged for Arif's explicit review.
evidence: Issue 01 Text, Section 3 vs Method Section 6

corrections.original_statement: In September 2026 both parties applied for separate hearings, which means the matter may split rather than resolve.
corrections.corrected_state: The petitions are scheduled to be heard in filing order. The petitions were not consolidated at the reported directions stage; the hearing panel will decide whether Sarawak's preliminary OIC issue should be heard first; both parties intended to request an enlarged panel of nine or eleven judges; Sarawak indicated an intended Rule 23 application. The claim that 'both parties applied for separate hearings' is UNVERIFIED; lack of consolidation does not warrant the inference that the matter may split.
corrections.reason: The statement asserted separate hearing applications and split proceedings as fact without primary court record verification.
corrections.consequence: Unverified procedural speculation presented as factual base case.
next_signals: 25-29 January 2027 hearing panel composition and order of arguments
